legal.privacy_description: What data Sena Studio uses, why, for how long, and how to exercise your rights.
legal.data_text: The form records your name and email address, project type, goal, timeline, and selected budget range. Phone number, organisation, and free-text message are optional. Replies and follow-up notes that may be added to the contact record can also be processed. The site uses a session cookie needed for its operation and to maintain navigation state. If audience measurement is enabled, your choice, the provider name, notice version, and a random identifier are kept for six months as evidence of the choice; this log is not linked to the contact form. To limit automated submissions, the request IP address is combined with the email as a temporary fingerprint used by the rate limiter for one hour. Hosting technical logs may contain connection data depending on provider configuration.
legal.purpose_text: This information is used to assess and handle your request, reply to you, and manage the exchange. The legal basis is taking steps at your request before entering a contract when you enquire about a potential engagement; for other professional enquiries, it is the legitimate interest in replying and managing correspondence. Rate limiting and abuse prevention rely on the legitimate interest in securing the form.
legal.storage_text: Contact records are kept for up to :years years from their creation, then removed by a daily purge task if Laravel's scheduler is active on the host. This period is not measured from the last exchange. Dashboard notifications containing the name, email, and subject are also removed with the record. The application is hosted by Railway and the database is provided by Supabase, in the eu-west-1 region according to the current configuration. Access is restricted to authorised administrator accounts. Notification email is sent through the configured mail service; no external email is sent in log mode. Cloudinary may process site files and images, not contact form fields. Fonts loaded from Bunny Fonts cause the visitor's browser to request that provider. Processing locations, any transfers, and retention periods for emails, logs, queues, or backups depend on provider configurations and contracts.
legal.rights_text: Subject to applicable rules and their conditions, you may request access, rectification, erasure, or restriction of processing, object to processing based on legitimate interests and, where the conditions are met, request data portability. To exercise a right or ask a question, email senadalmeidapro@gmail.com. A response is provided within the period required by applicable rules — one month where GDPR applies, with a possible extension for complex requests. Reasonable proof of identity may be requested if needed to protect your data. If you believe the processing does not comply with applicable rules, you may complain to the competent supervisory authority.
legal.privacy_confirmation_text: Sèna Gédéon D'ALMEIDA, who operates Sena Studio from Cotonou, Benin, determines the purposes and means of processing contact form data and acts as its controller. Required fields are needed to handle your request; without them, the form cannot be submitted. Optional fields may be left blank. Data is not sold. Applicable rules depend in particular on the people affected and the processing; this notice is not a compliance certification.

process.title: A clear path to reliable software
process.subtitle: Requirements before code. I clarify what the system needs to accomplish, shape the simplest design that fits, then validate each step against real constraints.
process.thesis: Start with the problem, not the technology.
process.lifecycle.title: The project lifecycle
process.lifecycle.text: A guiding workflow, not a one-way checklist. New evidence, tests or requirements can take the work back to an earlier decision.
process.stage_clarify.title: Clarify
process.stage_clarify.text: Agree on the need, the people affected and the boundaries of the work.
process.stage_design.title: Design
process.stage_design.text: Model the domain and choose a system that fits its real constraints.
process.stage_build.title: Build
process.stage_build.text: Plan, implement and verify the work in reviewable increments.
process.stage_deliver.title: Deliver
process.stage_deliver.text: Release carefully, observe the result and improve from evidence.
process.phase_1.title: Understand the problem
process.phase_1.text: Identify the business need, the people affected, the outcome they need and the constraints around it. Resolve open questions before choosing a technical solution.
process.phase_2.title: Define requirements and scope
process.phase_2.text: Make functional needs, quality requirements, priorities, exclusions and acceptance criteria explicit. Record assumptions when a decision still depends on missing information.
process.phase_3.title: Model the domain and data
process.phase_3.text: Describe the domain concepts, relationships, business rules and state changes. Then shape persistence around those needs, including consistency, transactions and important queries.
process.phase_4.title: Design the system
process.phase_4.text: Choose the simplest architecture that fits. Map the components and their interactions, then define the API, data boundaries and technical decisions with their trade-offs.
process.phase_5.title: Plan for failure and reliability
process.phase_5.text: Consider expected workload, unavailable dependencies, timeouts, concurrent changes and recovery. Add queues, caching or distributed components only when requirements or evidence justify them.
process.phase_6.title: Plan the implementation
process.phase_6.text: Break the design into prioritized features, dependencies and milestones. Give each task a clear completion condition so progress can be reviewed against the requirements.
process.phase_7.title: Implement in small increments
process.phase_7.text: Deliver one coherent vertical slice at a time: validate input, apply business rules, persist data and connect the interface. Review each feature before expanding the scope.
process.phase_8.title: Test and validate
process.phase_8.text: Check business logic, integrations, user journeys, permissions and acceptance criteria. Cover relevant edge cases, fix failures and rerun the checks that matter.
process.phase_9.title: Deploy and observe
process.phase_9.text: Prepare configuration and migrations, release in a controlled way, then verify health and essential workflows. Watch logs and operational signals, and keep a recovery path ready.
process.phase_10.title: Review and improve
process.phase_10.text: Compare the result with the original need. Use feedback, test results and operational evidence to simplify decisions, address worthwhile debt and guide the next iteration.
process.daily.title: A normal development day
process.daily.text: For a focused change, I use the same discipline at a smaller scale.
process.daily_1.title: Set the objective
process.daily_1.text: Name the feature, bug or risk to address.
process.daily_2.title: Inspect the current state
process.daily_2.text: Read the relevant code, tests and dependencies.
process.daily_3.title: Choose the change
process.daily_3.text: Find the cause and the smallest suitable solution.
process.daily_4.title: Implement
process.daily_4.text: Keep the change focused and preserve intended behavior.
process.daily_5.title: Verify
process.daily_5.text: Run relevant checks and examine edge cases.
process.daily_6.title: Review and record
process.daily_6.text: Check the diff and note decisions or remaining work.
process.principles.title: What guides the decisions
process.principles.text: The aim is the simplest reliable solution that meets the actual requirements.
process.principle_clarity.title: Clarity
process.principle_clarity.text: Resolve ambiguity before committing to a solution.
process.principle_structure.title: Structure
process.principle_structure.text: Make each phase produce a decision or artifact that can be reviewed.
process.principle_judgment.title: Technical judgment
process.principle_judgment.text: Choose tools and architecture to fit the requirements, and explain the trade-offs.
process.principle_depth.title: Practical depth
process.principle_depth.text: Account for failure, data consistency, security and operation.
process.principle_iteration.title: Iteration
process.principle_iteration.text: Test assumptions and adapt when evidence changes.
data_handling.title: Data handling
data_handling.subtitle: The business operates from Cotonou, Benin. Roles and applicable rules are determined for each engagement and the people affected. This page describes the general approach; it does not replace the contract or project-specific checks.
data_handling.client_data.title: Data involved in client work
data_handling.client_data.text: Data categories and operations are defined with the client before work begins. Where an engagement involves personal data processed on the client's behalf, documented instructions, each party's responsibilities, and security measures must be agreed in writing. Real data is used only when needed for the agreed scope; synthetic or minimised data should be preferred for development and testing.
data_handling.retention.title: Retention
data_handling.retention.text: Each engagement should specify how long data may be accessed, how it will be returned or deleted at the end of the work, and any client retention obligations. No universal period is promised here: it should be documented in the engagement terms and checked before any production data is accessed.
data_handling.subprocessors.title: Subprocessors
data_handling.subprocessors.text: Required tools and subprocessors depend on the project. Before processing data for a client, relevant providers, their functions, processing locations, and any transfers should be checked and disclosed in the contractual arrangement. Providers used by this portfolio site are described in its privacy policy; they are not automatically used for client projects.
data_handling.gdpr_contact.title: Data and privacy contact
data_handling.gdpr_contact.text: To discuss data needed for an engagement or ask a privacy question, contact Sèna Gédéon D'ALMEIDA at senadalmeidapro@gmail.com. Whether GDPR or other rules apply depends on the engagement, the people affected, and the territories involved; relevant requirements should be confirmed with the client and its qualified advisers.
